Is your NGINX front‑end truly safe? Researchers disclosed two critical HTTP/2 flaws on 18 November 2026, each scoring 9.2 on the CVSS scale.

The vulnerabilities, CVE‑2026‑123633 (use‑after‑free) and CVE‑2026‑123007 (integer underflow), affect every NGINX release from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 when HTTP/2 is enabled, allowing unauthenticated remote‑code execution.

A coordinated patch will arrive in version 1.31.9, but until then the only reliable mitigation is to disable HTTP/2 on affected listeners. The bugs have been present for over a decade, meaning most production deployments remain exposed.

“An unauthenticated attacker can run arbitrary code simply by sending a crafted HTTP/2 request.”  

Because NGINX sits at the front door of millions of sites and APIs, a compromise can give attackers full control over traffic, credentials, and downstream services.

The data reflects disclosures from multiple research groups and the upcoming F5 security release; the exact impact may vary by configuration.

How are you ensuring your NGINX instances are protected while the patch is pending?
